# The field notes

The reflections written on the walls of the endless museum, in walk order.

Each entry is one line of the book: the sentence a wall hangs, and under it what
was written standing in front of it. The line lives in
`commons/data/book/<chapter>.json` as `text`; the reflection is `note` on the same
line. Both are editable in the museum (click the wall, then the inspector), at
[/wall-map](http://localhost:3003/wall-map), [/wall-texts](http://localhost:3003/wall-texts)
and [/lines](http://localhost:3003/lines).

*Generated by `python tools/field_notes.py --apply`. Do not edit this file — edit
the book, and run it again.*

**270 reflections** across 269 halls in 24 chapters — 53,959 characters, out of 843 lines in the book.

## array_tutorial

### tutorial single · `Tutorial_Single`

**`xyz_coordinates`**

> *Cartesian coordinate system, x y z godot*

a single cube has no index: one object cannot say where it is, so the map lends it a frame — and the gadget's right angles and unit lengths get read as properties of space rather than one convention.

### tutorial pattern · `Tutorial_Pattern`

**`panel_bridge_loom`**

> *Three interactive VR panels displaying a weaving draft*

the drawdown is the one panel you cannot edit: no thread in the cloth is addressable, only the two orders above it, so the diagonal you want has to be argued for upstream and never placed.

### array patterns · `Array_Patterns`

**`tiling_demo`**

> *a tiling motif is a function from grid index to visual element*

a repeat needs a plane that will accept it, and the plane accepts exactly seventeen grammars — no eighteenth, no five-fold rosette; Casa del Fauno and the Cosmatesque floors are instances, never additions.

### tutorial row · `Tutorial_Row`

**`column_3_z`**

> *an array is space made countable — column_3_z makes the abstract concept of an index into a physical position you can walk …*

the row cannot say which cube is [0] — an index is a count from an end somebody chose, so the pink tags are borrowed, and lifting a cube leaves a hole that keeps counting.

### tutorial 2d build · `Tutorial_2D_Build`

**`pulsar_visualizer`**

> *the first discovered pulsar was initially called LGM-1 (Little Green Men) because the signal's regularity seemed artificial*

the grid can address any cell but cannot decide what belongs in one: the pulsar arrives continuous and is cut at 0.25 — below the line the star stops existing, and the remainder reads as engineered.

### tutorial 3d · `Tutorial_3D`

**`grid_3d_4x4x4`**

> *a three-dimensional array is the minimum structure needed to represent volumetric space*

a filled 4×4×4 has no readable inside: the inner indices reach the eye only because every label is drawn with depth testing off, through the cubes in front of it, and reach the hand only by emptying them.

arrangement is not authorship until something else must route around it: the chamber fires nothing, so it borrows the agent's plan to make a placed block mean anything, and the meaning arrives as extra steps.

## boolean_surfaces

### boolean union · `Boolean_Union`

**`csg_union_demo`**

> *Union is the generous operator. It keeps everything either shape claims*

union depends on a yes/no crossing test with no middle: at one float the solids are two, at the next they are one — and the seam it advertises as dissolved is the curve it had to compute first.

### boolean intersection · `Boolean_Intersection`

**`csg_intersection_demo`**

> *Intersection is the shape of consensus. What both shapes agree on is always less than either …*

intersection depends on an interior the renderer never draws, and it is the one operator whose lawful answer can be nothing: two solids that miss return the empty solid, indistinguishable from a build that failed.

### boolean difference · `Boolean_Difference`

**`csg_difference_demo`**

> *To make a room, subtract a void from a solid. Architecture is difference*

difference depends on a face neither solid brought: the cavity wall is B inverted, and it can only be dressed in A's outer skin — a boundary model stores no interior, so the carved inside is the outside, relabelled.

### boolean compose workbench · `Boolean_Compose_Workbench`

**`csg_compose_workbench`**

> *Three operators, one algebra. Composition is a choice*

the bench calls three operators an algebra, but the three are an enum on a Godot property: the set is what the engine exposes, not what the algebra holds — no complement, no XOR, closure bought by leaving them out.

### boolean · `Chamber_Boolean`  *(dropped)*

*the hall itself*

the chamber's verb is to compose, and composition needs an order the finished solid cannot keep: the block handed back has no memory of which verb came first, so the room depends on you remembering.

### boolean architecture cavity · `Boolean_Architecture_Cavity`  *(dropped)*

*the hall itself*

the map claims a room is a wall subtracted from, but one difference makes a hole, not an inside: an interior needs three more runs of solid the map never places — the payoff is read from outside.

## cellularautomata

### ca introduction · `CA_Introduction`

**`grid_substrate_runner`**

> *an integrated substrate edits the floor that's already there*

the floor is the automaton, and a floor must be crossable: a BFS refills whatever the pattern killed between spawn and teleporter, so the first rule the learner meets has already been overruled by the need to carry them.

### ca elementaryrules · `CA_ElementaryRules`

**`structure_growth`**

> *3D structure growth simulation*

the argument is that 256 is small enough to walk: eight bits enumerate every rule, and a room cannot hold 256 walls, so one 26-neighbour 3D automaton stands where the enumeration should be and completeness stays a claim.

### ca gameoflife · `CA_GameOfLife`

**`ca_bridge`**

> *A bridge built by a rule — you walk on computation*

you walk on computation, and no three-cell rule knows it owes you a floor: rule 110 computes and fills 49.7% of the deck, rule 250 fills 87.5% and computes nothing — the crossing costs the argument.

### ca beyondbinary · `CA_BeyondBinary`

**`ca_growth_network`**

> *Growth toward a goal, with noise, is enough to produce every vascular pattern in nature*

the vascular claim needs somewhere to grow toward: eight attractors are placed before the first tip moves, so the growth stays local only because the global information was smuggled in ahead of it as goals nobody grew.

### ca expandingspace · `CA_ExpandingSpace`

**`decaying_bridge`**

> *Architecture that reacts to presence is architecture that is alive*

reacting to presence is not a local rule: every tick the bridge asks the whole scene tree for a node in group "player" and decays within two cells of the answer — the reach that matters is a lookup, not a neighbourhood.

### ca softrules · `CA_SoftRules`

**`ca_sphere`**

> *The same rules on a sphere produce forms no flat grid ever could*

"the same rules" needs the same neighbourhood everywhere, and a sphere has none to give: this one is a 64-by-32 lat-long mesh, crowded at the poles and thin at the equator, so the automaton's world is the mesher's.

### ca agentscircuits · `CA_AgentsCircuits`

**`sierpinski_pyramid`**

> *Five copies of yourself, arranged just so, and you contain yourself forever*

authorship over the rule is the payoff and no procedure comes with it: nothing runs from a wanted behaviour back to a rule number, so writing a rule here is searching 256 of them and looking.

### ca · `Chamber_CA`  *(dropped)*

*the hall itself*

two rule systems meet and neither can say who won: Conway keeps no score, so the chamber imports one — a perturbation that outlives a few ticks counts as a contribution, and the clock does the judging.

### ca edgeofchaos · `CA_EdgeOfChaos`

**`self_organization_ca`**

> *There are two ways to die — freeze into one thing*

narrowness can only be shown by leaving the band, and nothing here can leave: lambda is a constant 0.5 with no slider in the map, so the edge of chaos is walked from inside it and the two deaths stay named, not met.

## foundationscrisis

### euclid parallel · `Euclid_Parallel`

**`angle_sum_triangle`**

> *the angle sum of a triangle is not a fact about triangles but a fact about the space they …*

the triangle cannot supply its own angle sum — 180° is a fact about the space, and the space arrives as a postulate every proof uses and no proof produces: certainty standing on a decision, not a truth.

### noneuclidean spaces · `NonEuclidean_Spaces`

**`poincare_disk`**

> *infinity can be contained in a finite disk — the Poincare model proves that hyperbolic geometry is as consistent as …*

hyperbolic space cannot be drawn honestly: the disk buys a finite picture of infinity by crushing the metric toward the rim, so every equal step outward is drawn smaller and the boundary is infinity rendered as a wall.

### russell paradox · `Russell_Paradox`

**`self_membership_set`**

> *The set that contains itself, all the way down - R = {x : x not-in x}, is R in R?*

a set that contains itself cannot supply its own bottom: the nest is only legible because someone cut it at five, and that cut — foundation, types, a levels export — is the restriction the paradox extorted.

### godel incompleteness · `Godel_Incompleteness`

**`godel_sentence_machine`**

> *if G were provable it would be false (it asserts its own unprovability)*

the machine builds G out of its own rules but cannot supply the standpoint from which G reads true — the gold verdict is spoken from outside, on a soundness no arm inside can reach.

### escher impossible · `Escher_Impossible`

**`escher_staircase`**

> *locally coherent does not mean globally possible*

an impossible figure cannot supply its own coherence: it depends on the one standpoint where the loop appears to close, and pays by hiding the joint — the fourth side quietly eased to zero where nobody looks.

### brouwer intuitionism · `Brouwer_Intuitionism`

**`constructive_proof`**

> *existence without construction is an article of faith, not a proof*

existence here cannot be asserted, only produced: the proof depends on somebody building the witness in time, and pays in everything true but unbuilt — the platforms that trail off are not false, they are unconstructed.

*the hall itself*

no test inside the chamber tells the two ghosts apart, so undecidability only becomes legible on a screen bolted to the wall: the lesson needs the outside view the fight forbids, or it reads as bad aim.

### florensky paraconsistent · `Florensky_Paraconsistent`

**`schrodinger_box`**

> *observation does not reveal a pre-existing state — it creates one*

the box cannot show what it holds — superposition needs the lid shut — so its only freedom is where to put the part it cannot display: sealed in the core, split to a twin, smeared into haze.
